thread:
customer-jane: Hi, we're getting a lot of streaming disconnects on /v1/stream. After ~60s of idle the client sees a partial chunk then reconnects. We also saw a billing spike due to reconnect loops and some reconnect attempts return 401s. Any ideas?

alex: Sorry to hear that — can you share the topology? ALB/NLB/Cloudflare/nginx/Envoy in front? Are you using HTTP/1.1 SSE or h2?

customer-jane: Topology = Cloudflare (WAF) -> AWS ALB -> Envoy sidecars -> redwood pod. Clients in EU. We use SSE (text/event-stream) over HTTP/1.1. Token is short-lived (45s) and gets rotated client-side.

alex: Two likely culprits: (1) ALB idle timeout default 60s closing the connection on idle; (2) Cloudflare or Envoy buffering/keepalive interactions causing midstream truncation. The 401 on reconnect sounds like token rotation race.

ingress-sre: Quick checks: share ALB access logs and Envoy access logs around the disconnect timestamps, and a tcpdump if you can. Also confirm ALB idle timeout (console or CLI) and whether Cloudflare is fronting in "Full" vs "Bypass" origin mode.

customer-jane: I attached the ALB logs snippet (pasted below). Timestamp ~2026-03-14T11:23:05Z.

support-bot: ALB log entry: "type=HTTP elb=app/redwood-alb/abcd client:port=3.4.5.6:52344 target:port=10.0.2.3:8080 request_processing_time=0.001 target_processing_time=59.999 response_processing_time=0.000 elb_status_code=504 target_status_code=502"

maria: That target_processing_time ~60s aligns with ALB default idle. If the app doesn't send heartbeats, ALB will cut. Envoy might then half-close causing the client to get a partial chunk.

alex: Repro steps to mimic on client locally:
```bash
# long-poll SSE with no heartbeat
TOKEN=<short_lived_token>
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```
If token rotates during reconnect, you can see 401 on the new connection.

ingress-sre: Suggested mitigations (order of preference):
- Server: emit a small comment/heartbeat every 20-30s (SSE comment `: ping\n\n`). This prevents ALB idle close.
- ALB: increase idle timeout to 300s if heartbeats are not possible (aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes).
- Envoy: set `stream_idle_timeout` or keepalive settings so it doesn't close server side at 60s.
- Cloudflare: enable "Origin keepalive" and disable buffering for the streaming endpoint (page rules or bypass).
- Nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_ignore_client_abort on;` for the location.

maria: Also for the 401/reconnect billing spike: don't rely on per-request short token rotation during a long-lived connection. Options:
- Use a long-lived connection token or session cookie for the duration of the SSE.
- Allow clients to perform a short re-auth during reconnect (refresh token flow) — server should accept `Last-Event-ID` header to resume idempotently.

customer-jane: We can add heartbeats quickly. But we still want infra to check ALB/Cloudflare behavior; if Cloudflare buffers, heartbeats might be coalesced and won't reach ALB.

alex: Good point. Cloudflare will buffer/optimize HTTP/1.1 often. For true streaming, ensure Cloudflare is set to not buffer the endpoint (set a rule to bypass caching and disable response buffering). Also confirm that Cloudflare is not upgrading to h2 between client and edge; h2 + buffering can change chunk behavior.

ingress-sre: Action items:
- customer-jane: deploy heartbeat in server (small SSE comment every 20s) and confirm client sees continuous events.
- infra (ingress-sre): check ALB attributes (idle timeout), ALB target group health/502 traces, and Cloudflare page rules for buffering.
- auth: review token rotation strategy for streaming, propose session-scoped token or refresh handshake on reconnect.

maria: Example Envoy config snippet to keep streams alive:
```yaml
http_connection_manager:
  common_http_protocol_options:
    idle_timeout: 0s # disable Envoy idle disconnects for long lived streams (use with care)
  stream_idle_timeout: 0s
```
And for nginx: `proxy_buffering off;` under the location for /v1/stream.

customer-jane: Will try heartbeat deploy now and report back. Quick Q: any immediate quick fix to stop billing spike?

alex: Temporary workaround: rate-limit reconnects at the CDN or edge (Cloudflare rate limiting) so a client stuck in a tight reconnect loop won't generate infinite tokens. Also set a short server-side dedupe window for identical client IDs so repeated reconnects within e.g., 10s are merged.

support-bot: Noted. Opening internal ticket #INC-2026-314 for infra trace and proposed ALB config change.

customer-jane: Thanks — heartbeat deployed, I can confirm client now receives a comment every 20s. We'll monitor for a few hours and then check billing + logs.

alex: Great. Follow-up: if you still see truncation after heartbeat, paste packet capture (tcpdump -s 0 -w stream.pcap) and we can look at where bytes get dropped (edge vs backend). :thumbsup:

customer-jane: Got it, thanks everyone.
